recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6928 unless PA or a later tracker reopens the broader jurisdiction-specific demographic data policy.
issue_request: FHIR-6928 was a Published FHIR-core Patient change request asking to make race and ethnicity optional core Patient elements. The PA work group resolved it as Not Persuasive with Modification: do not add these concepts to base Patient; instead add Patient introduction guidance that such concepts vary by jurisdiction and belong in profiles or standard extensions.
initial_application: Commit c68d4605860158d67a4b62863a313b001a3c92b2, titled 'Tracker #6928, 7301...', added the Patient introduction paragraph about race, ethnicity, organ donor status, nationality, jurisdictional profiles, and standard extensions. Later line history corrected spelling/punctuation and updated the standard-extensions link to patient-core.html while preserving the substance.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists patient=Patient under [resources], confirming the Patient resource source is in current build scope. Current source/patient/patient-introduction.xml lines 28-31 contain the resolved guidance. Jira search also found FHIR-7114, a duplicate of the same request, and FHIR-7301, a separate Patient birthDate/birthTime issue named in the same historical commit and already represented on the combined branch. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant or conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding race/ethnicity elements would contradict the Not Persuasive with Modification decision, and adding more explanatory prose would be redundant with the existing Patient introduction paragraph.
